# Installation

SEALS is published on conda-forge as the package `sealsmodel` (the name `seals`
was already taken; you still `import seals`). One `mamba install` gives you SEALS,
hazelbean and the whole geospatial stack as prebuilt binaries for Windows, macOS
and Linux. No compiler and no clone are needed.

The [developer install](#developer-install) below, an editable install from a
clone of the repository, is still the right choice if you intend to change SEALS
itself. For everyone else, the conda-forge package is the install.

## 1. Install Miniforge

If not already installed: **Miniforge** — <https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge>.
Install for your user account only, and accept the option to add it to your
`PATH`. Miniforge ships both `conda` and `mamba` and is preconfigured to use the
conda-forge channel, which is where `sealsmodel` lives.

## 2. Create and activate an environment

```bash
conda create -n <your_env>
conda activate <your_env>
```

Pick your own environment name — the devstack does not require a particular one.
Always activate it before running SEALS scripts.

The environment starts empty on purpose; Python arrives in step 3 as a dependency
of `sealsmodel`, at a version conda knows the package was built for.

## 3. Install SEALS from conda-forge

```bash
mamba install sealsmodel
```

This is the whole install. The solve may take several minutes the first time
because it brings in hazelbean, GDAL, NumPy and the rest of the stack as conda
builds. `conda install sealsmodel` works too, just more slowly.

## 4. Verify

```bash
python -c "import seals, hazelbean; print(seals.__file__)"
```

A path inside your environment's `site-packages` is the expected answer for this
install. Then go to [Quickstart](quickstart.qmd), which makes a first run from a
project folder of your own.

To upgrade later, run `mamba update sealsmodel` in the activated environment.

## Developer install {#developer-install}

Use this when you want to edit SEALS and see the change the next time you run
it: an *editable install* of a clone, with the Cython extension compiled on your
machine. It replaces step 3 above; steps 1 and 2 still apply.

### a. Install git and a C/C++ compiler

- **git** — <https://git-scm.com/downloads>. The install starts from a clone.
- SEALS compiles a Cython extension (`seals/seals_cython_functions.pyx`) when it
  is installed from source, so **a C/C++ compiler is required** — see
  [Compiling C/C++ Code](https://justinandrewjohnson.com/earth_economy_devstack/installation.html#compiling-cc-code).
  - **macOS:** `xcode-select --install`
  - **Windows:** Visual Studio Build Tools, or run `install.bat` from the
    Earth-Economy Devstack repository root
  - **Linux:** `gcc` is usually already present

### b. Get the dependency stack from conda-forge

The clone needs hazelbean, GDAL, NumPy and friends as conda builds, not pip
wheels. Either install `sealsmodel` and then remove just the package, keeping
everything it pulled in:

```bash
mamba install sealsmodel
conda remove sealsmodel --force
```

or install the dependencies directly:

```bash
mamba install hazelbean cython libgdal-hdf5
```

Removing the package is what keeps a packaged copy from shadowing your clone.
Use `conda remove --force`, not `pip uninstall`: conda owns the package, and pip
leaves zombie folders behind.

### c. Clone SEALS into the devstack layout

You may clone SEALS wherever you want, but the documentation assumes the repo
lives in its own project folder under `~/Files/`
(`C:\Users\<you>\Files\` on Windows). The command below clones it into a `seals`
subfolder there.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/Files/seals && cd ~/Files/seals
git clone https://github.com/jandrewjohnson/seals.git
```

The second `seals` is the repository itself. Projects, and everything SEALS
writes, go beside it in the first `seals`.

### d. Make the editable install

```bash
cd ~/Files/seals/seals
pip install -e . --no-deps
```

`--no-deps` is deliberate, and required. SEALS declares `hazelbean>=2.1.0` as its
only runtime dependency, and you already have it from step b. Letting pip resolve
dependencies again tends to replace conda's builds of the geospatial stack (GDAL
and friends) with incompatible wheels.

### e. Verify

```bash
python -c "import seals; print(seals.__file__)"
```

For this install the path must be inside your clone, not under `site-packages`.
If it is under `site-packages`, a packaged copy is shadowing the clone: remove it
as in step b and redo the editable install.

### Other devstack repos (optional)

The same clone-and-editable-install pattern works for the rest of the stack, each
in its own `~/Files/<name>/` project folder:
[global_invest_dev](https://github.com/NatCapTEEMs/global_invest_dev),
[gtap_invest_dev](https://github.com/jandrewjohnson/gtap_invest_dev),
[gtappy_dev](https://github.com/jandrewjohnson/gtappy_dev),
[gep_dev](https://github.com/jandrewjohnson/gep_dev).
All but `global_invest_dev` are private; ask for read access before cloning them.

See the [full installation guide](https://justinandrewjohnson.com/earth_economy_devstack/installation.html)
for the devstack-wide version of these steps, including the hazelbean clone.

## Troubleshooting

The devstack guide's
[Common problems](https://justinandrewjohnson.com/earth_economy_devstack/installation.html#common-problems)
section covers the environment-level failures, none of which are SEALS-specific:
you need administrator rights; PowerShell needs `conda init powershell` before
conda works in it; conda may need adding to `PATH` manually; and Windows may show
"Windows protected your PC" on the Miniforge installer (click *More info* → *Run
anyway*).

If you made the developer install and `import seals` resolves to
`site-packages`, see [step e](#developer-install) — an installed copy is
shadowing your clone.

If an import fails on Windows 11 with `ImportError: DLL load failed ... An
Application Control policy has blocked this file`, Windows **Smart App Control**
is blocking a compiled extension (statsmodels' and SEALS' own, among others) in
the newly created environment. It is a per-machine Windows Security setting
(*App & browser control*), not an install error, and it blocks any unsigned
binary conda unpacks; turning it off is the fix, but note that Windows does not
allow it to be switched back on without a reinstall.

## Next

With the environment activated, go to [Quickstart](quickstart.qmd) — it runs the
pared test pipeline and shows where the output lands.

Budget time for the first run rather than the install: SEALS downloads the base
data it needs at runtime from a public bucket, so a correct install is still
followed by a substantial download before you see a result. No credentials are
needed for the default configuration.
